channel.title: Recommended Reading on metafunctor
channel.description: Curated reading lists extending the metafunctor series. Each list pairs with a series under /series/ and covers the canonical literature of that topic: the books, papers, courses, and tools I would hand someone starting out.

item.title: Minds and Machines: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The canonical literature on AI safety, mesa-optimization, interpretability, and the philosophical foundations of alignment. Curated to extend the Minds and Machines series.

item.title: RL Assumptions: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Reinforcement learning foundations, deep RL, and the universal-agent literature that frames representation choices as priors. Curated to extend the RL Assumptions series.

item.title: Sequential Prediction: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The canonical literature on information theory, context-tree weighting, universal prediction, and neural sequence modeling. Curated to extend the Sequential Prediction series.

item.title: SICP: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: SICP, its successors, and the Lisp and programming-language literature that makes computation-as-a-medium-for-ideas the central concern.

item.title: Statistical Reliability: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The canonical literature on survival analysis, parametric reliability, competing risks with masked causes, likelihood theory, and the R software stack, curated to extend the Statistical Reliability series.

item.title: Stepanov: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The Stepanov canon and the generic-programming, functional-algebra, C++, and type-theory literature that supports it. Curated to extend the Stepanov series.

item.title: The Learning Problem: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The canonical literature on universal induction, Bayesian inference, statistical learning theory, and the Minimum Description Length principle. Curated to extend The Learning Problem series.

item.title: The Long Echo: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The Unix-philosophy canon, digital-preservation literature, and the memex-to-personal-knowledge-archive lineage that underpins the Long Echo toolkit.

item.title: Trapdoor Computing: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The canonical literature on searchable encryption, oblivious RAM and access-pattern hiding, approximate set data structures, and the information-theoretic foundations that trapdoor computing builds on.
